questions.q: As of March 2023, how many High Courts are there in India?
questions.solution:

• ​The institution of the high court originated in India in 1862 with three high courts set up at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.

• The fourth HC was established in Allahabad in 1866.

• Currently, India has a total of 25 High Courts established in different states of the country.

• The Andhra Pradesh High Court became the 25th High Court of India when it was established on January 1, 2019.

• The UTs of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh have a common high court.

• Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the organisation, independence, jurisdiction, powers, procedures and so on of the HC.

• The Seventh Amendment Act of 1956 authorised the Parliament to establish a common HC for two or more states or two or more states and a UT

questions.q: Which species is known as black lipped pearl oyster found in the Indo-Pacific, within tropical coral reefs?

• Pinctada margaritifera, commonly known as the black-lipped pearl oyster, is a bivalve mollusc belonging to the family Pteriidae

• It is widely distributed in the Indo-Pacific region, particularly within tropical coral reef ecosystems.

• These environments provide the optimal conditions for its survival, including warm water temperatures and an abundance of plankton for food.

• The term "black-lipped" refers to the distinct dark colouration found on the inner edges of its shell.

• This feature distinguishes it from other pearl oysters.

• This species is particularly valued in the pearl industry as it is a primary producer of high-quality Tahitian black pearls, which are renowned for their unique colours and lustre.

• Like other bivalves, it filters water for food, contributing to the clarity and health of its marine environment.

• It also serves as a habitat for various small marine organisms.

Additional Information

• Also known as the spotted sea hare, it is a sea slug.

• These animals are known for their soft, wrinkled bodies, which can have various colours and patterns, including spots.

• They have a distinct head region with tentacles, and their bodies are somewhat flattened.

• Dentalium neohexagonum:

• A species of scaphopod mollusk, also known as a tusk shell

• Scaphopods are marine molluscs that have tubular, tapered shells that are open at both ends.

• These shells resemble the shape of an elephant’s tusk, which is how they got the name "tusk shell."

• Chatepleura apiculata:

questions.q: The CSO adopted the concept of Gross Value Added in _.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is January 2015 Key Points

• The Central Statistics Office (CSO) adopted the concept of Gross Value Added (GVA) in January 2015 as part of a major revision in the national accounts statistics.

• This change was implemented when the base year for GDP calculation was shifted from 2004-05 to 2011-12.

• GVA measures the contribution of each sector to the economy.

• It reflects the value of goods and services produced in an economy after deducting the cost of inputs and raw materials.

• This adoption aligns India's statistical calculations with international practices and standards like those recommended by the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA).

• Along with the introduction of GVA, the base year revision to 2011-12 was applied to GDP estimates.

• This revision ensured more accurate and updated data representation, helping policymakers assess economic performance better.

• It was controversial for its time because it challenged Hindu religious scriptures as a source of women's oppression.

• She was a member of the Satyashodhak Samaj and an associate of Savitribai Phule and Jyotirao Phule

• She was the daughter of Debendranath Tagore and the sister of Rabindranath Tagore.

• Her work advocated for women's education and empowerment during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

• Pandita Ramabai

• A social reformer and educationist who worked extensively for women's rights and education, especially for widows in India.

• She founded the Arya Mahila Samaj and the Mukti Mission for destitute women.

• She was one of the earliest proponents of women's education in colonial India and a pioneering feminist figure.

• A prominent freedom fighter and Gandhian.

• Famous for running the Congress Radio, an underground radio station, during the Quit India Movement (1942) to broadcast messages against British rule.

questions.q: Which physical feature of India prevents the cold winds from central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinents?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Himalayas Key Points

• The Himalayas are the physical feature that prevents cold winds from Central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinent

• The Himalayas are a lofty mountain range that blocks cold winds from Central Asia from entering India.

• The Himalayas' height, location, and complex topography significantly impact the climate of the Indian subcontinent.

• The Himalayas also influence the monsoons, forcing the rain-bearing winds to lose most of their moisture before crossing the range.

• The Himalayas cause the Indian subcontinent to experience milder winters than Central Asia.

• Northern India also has higher temperatures than other areas on the same latitudes.

Additional Information

• Indian plains

• The Northern Plains, also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plain, are the granaries of India and the foundation for early civilizations.

• This vast plain is formed by the rivers Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, and their tributaries.

• It stretches across northern and northeastern India, covering states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Punjab, Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh.

• The Indo-Gangetic plain is characterized by fertile soils, making it one of the most important agricultural regions in India.

• It is densely populated, with major cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Lucknow, and Patna located along its course.

• Indian desert

• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is India's largest desert, covering about 77,000 square miles.

• The Thar Desert spans across parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana in India, extending into Pakistan.

• It covers around 200,000 square kilometres in India, primarily in the state of Rajasthan.

• The desert supports sparse vegetation like cactus, acacia trees, and scrub plants.

• Coastal areas

• India's coastal areas include the coastal states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal, as well as the coastal union territories of Daman & Diu, Puducherry, Lakshadweep Islands, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

• Coastal plains are low-lying, flat areas of land that are adjacent to the sea or ocean.

• The elevation of the land increases gradually from the sea to the highlands.

• India's other main physical features include the Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions about the organisation of 'Village Panchayats'?

• Article 40 of the Indian Constitution mentions the organization of village panchayats

• Article 40 of the Constitution states that the state shall take steps to organize village panchayats and give them the powers and authority to function as units of self-government.

• Article 40 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are guidelines for framing laws and policies.

• The DPSP is in Part IV of the Constitution, Articles 36–51.

• Panchayati raj

• The Panchayati raj system is a system of local self-government for villages in rural India.

• It includes the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), which are responsible for:

• Economic development

• Strengthening social justice

• Implementing Central and State Government Schemes

Additional Information

• Article 36

• This article of the Statute of the International Court of Justice defines the Court's jurisdiction.

• It states that the Court's jurisdiction includes all cases referred to it by the parties, as well as matters specified in the Charter of the United Nations, treaties, and conventions.

• Article 38

• Respecting international humanitarian law in armed conflicts

questions.q: Find the values of x, y and z, so as to satisfy the equations given below: x + y + z = 12; x + y – z = 6; x – y + z = 4
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Subtracting the second equation from the first gives 2z = 12 − 6 ⇒ z = 3.

Subtracting the third equation from the first gives 2y = 12 − 4 ⇒ y = 4.

Substituting y = 4 and z = 3 in the first equation gives x = 12 − 4 − 3 = 5.

∴ The correct answer is x = 5, y = 4, z = 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

x + y + z = 12 ...... (i)

x + y − z = 6 ...... (ii)

x − y + z = 4 ...... (iii)

Calculations:

⇒ Subtracting equation (ii) from equation (i):

⇒ (x + y + z) − (x + y − z) = 12 − 6

⇒ x + y + z − x − y + z = 6

⇒ 2z = 6

⇒ z = 3

⇒ Subtracting equation (iii) from equation (i):

⇒ (x + y + z) − (x − y + z) = 12 − 4

⇒ x + y + z − x + y − z = 8

⇒ 2y = 8

⇒ y = 4

⇒ Substituting the values of y and z in equation (i):

⇒ x + 4 + 3 = 12

⇒ x + 7 = 12

⇒ x = 5

∴ The correct answer is x = 5, y = 4, z = 3.

Additional Information

Elimination Method

This involves adding or subtracting equations to eliminate a variable, simplifying the system to fewer variables for straightforward calculation.

Substitution Method

One variable is isolated in one equation and substituted into the others, reducing the number of unknowns step by step until a single variable is found.

Cramer's Rule

A matrix-based method that uses determinants to solve a system of linear equations, applicable specifically when the determinant of the main coefficient matrix is non-zero.

questions.q: A policeman noticed a thief at a distance of 500 metres. The policeman started running and the thief also started running at the same time. The thief is running at a speed of 15 km/h. It took 15 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the speed of the policeman (in km/h).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative speed = Distance gap ÷ Time taken to catch

Initial Distance gap = 500 m = 0.5 km, Time taken = 15 mins = 1/4 hour.

Relative speed = 0.5 ÷ (1/4) = 2 km/h.

Since both are moving in the same direction, Policeman's speed = Thief's speed + Relative speed.

Policeman's speed = 15 + 2 = 17 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 17 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial distance between the policeman and the thief = 500 m = 0.5 km

Speed of the thief = 15 km/h

Time taken to catch the thief = 15 minutes = 15/60 hours = 1/4 hours



Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed of Object 1 − Speed of Object 2

Calculations:

Let the speed of the policeman be P km/h.

⇒ Distance covered by the thief before getting caught = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance covered by the thief = 15 × (1/4) = 3.75 km

⇒ Total distance covered by the policeman = Initial gap + Distance covered by the thief

⇒ Total distance covered by policeman = 0.5 km + 3.75 km = 4.25 km

⇒ Speed of policeman (P) = Total Distance ÷ Time taken

⇒ P = 4.25 ÷ (1/4)

⇒ P = 4.25 × 4

⇒ P = 17 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 17 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies travel in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated as the difference between their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies travel in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is calculated as the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion Trick

To quickly convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.q: If A:B = 6:8 and B:C = 5:12, then A:B:C is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the inverted N-method to combine ratios a:b and c:d:

A : B : C = (a × c) : (b × c) : (b × d)

Here, a:b = 6:8 and c:d = 5:12

⇒ A : B : C = (6 × 5) : (8 × 5) : (8 × 12)

⇒ A : B : C = 30 : 40 : 96 ⇒ 15 : 20 : 48

Alternate Method

Given:

A : B = 6 : 8

B : C = 5 : 12

Method Used:

To combine two ratios, make the common term (B) equal by finding the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of its values in both ratios.



Calculations:

⇒ First, simplify A : B = 6 : 8 = 3 : 4

⇒ Now we have B : C = 5 : 12

⇒ The common term B has values 4 and 5 in the respective ratios.

⇒ LCM of 4 and 5 = 20

⇒ Multiply A : B by 5 to make B equal to 20:

⇒ A : B = (3 × 5) : (4 × 5) = 15 : 20

⇒ Multiply B : C by 4 to make B equal to 20:

⇒ B : C = (5 × 4) : (12 × 4) = 20 : 48

⇒ Combining the ratios, A : B : C = 15 : 20 : 48

∴ The correct answer is 15:20:48.

Additional Information

Compound Ratio

For two given ratios a:b and c:d, the compound ratio is calculated by multiplying the antecedent and consequent respectively as (a × c) : (b × d).

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a ratio a:b is given by the square of its terms, which is a² : b².

Invertendo Property

If two ratios a:b and c:d are in strict proportion (a:b = c:d), then by invertendo property, b:a = d:c.

Componendo & Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This fundamental property is heavily used to quickly simplify complex fractional equations in ratio and proportion.

questions.q: If 2 tan θ = 3, then ((3 sin θ - 2 cos θ))/((3 sin θ + 2 cos θ)) is equal to:

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Divide the numerator and the denominator of the given expression by cos θ.

⇒ (3 tan θ − 2) / (3 tan θ + 2)

Given 2 tan θ = 3 ⇒ tan θ = 3/2.

Substitute tan θ = 3/2 into the simplified expression:

⇒ [3 × (3/2) − 2] / [3 × (3/2) + 2] = (9/2 − 2) / (9/2 + 2) = (5/2) / (13/2) = 5/13

∴ The correct answer is 5/13.

Alternate Method

Given:

2 tan θ = 3 ⇒ tan θ = 3/2

Formula Used:

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse

Calculations:

⇒ Let Perpendicular (P) = 3 and Base (B) = 2

⇒ Hypotenuse (H) = √(P² + B²) = √(3² + 2²) = √(9 + 4) = √13

⇒ sin θ = P/H = 3/√13

⇒ cos θ = B/H = 2/√13

⇒ Expression = (3 sin θ − 2 cos θ) / (3 sin θ + 2 cos θ)

⇒ Substitute the values of sin θ and cos θ:

⇒ [3 × (3/√13) − 2 × (2/√13)] / [3 × (3/√13) + 2 × (2/√13)]

⇒ (9/√13 − 4/√13) / (9/√13 + 4/√13)

⇒ (5/√13) / (13/√13)

⇒ 5/13

∴ The correct answer is 5/13.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios

The fundamental ratios in a right-angled triangle are: sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

Quotient Identities

The tangent and cotangent functions can be expressed in terms of sine and cosine: tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ and cot θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ.

Pythagorean Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².

questions.q: If p cos A = 2q sin A and 2p cosec A - q sec A = 3, then the value of p² + 4q² is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

From p cos A = 2q sin A, we can write p = 2k sin A and q = k cos A.

Substitute these in 2p cosec A − q sec A = 3, using cosec A = 1 / sin A and sec A = 1 / cos A:

⇒ 2(2k sin A) / sin A − (k cos A) / cos A = 3

⇒ 4k − k = 3 ⇒ 3k = 3 ⇒ k = 1

⇒ p² + 4q² = (2(1) sin A)² + 4(1 cos A)² = 4 sin² A + 4 cos² A = 4(1) = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

p cos A = 2q sin A --- (1)

2p cosec A − q sec A = 3 --- (2)

Formula Used:

cosec A = 1 / sin A

sec A = 1 / cos A

sin² A + cos² A = 1

Calculations:

From equation (1), we can express q in terms of p:

⇒ q = (p cos A) / (2 sin A)

Substitute the value of q in equation (2):

⇒ (2p / sin A) − [ (p cos A) / (2 sin A) ] × (1 / cos A) = 3

⇒ (2p / sin A) − (p / 2 sin A) = 3

⇒ (4p − p) / (2 sin A) = 3

⇒ 3p / 2 sin A = 3

⇒ p / 2 sin A = 1

⇒ p = 2 sin A

Now, substitute p = 2 sin A back into equation (1):

⇒ (2 sin A) cos A = 2q sin A

⇒ q = cos A

Now, calculate the value of p² + 4q²:

⇒ p² + 4q² = (2 sin A)² + 4(cos A)²

⇒ p² + 4q² = 4 sin² A + 4 cos² A

⇒ p² + 4q² = 4(sin² A + cos² A)

Since sin² A + cos² A = 1:

⇒ p² + 4q² = 4 × 1 = 4

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

The most commonly used identity linking sine and cosine is sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, which holds true for all valid angles θ.

Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios

The reciprocal of sine is cosecant (cosec θ = 1 / sin θ) and the reciprocal of cosine is secant (sec θ = 1 / cos θ).

Quotient Trigonometric Ratios

Tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine (tan θ = sin θ / cos θ) while cotangent is its reciprocal (cot θ = cos θ / sin θ).

When two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal.

Calculation:

⇒ ΔEFG ∼ ΔHIJ

⇒ EF / HI = FG / IJ = EG / HJ

⇒ We know that 3EF = HI, so EF / HI = 1 / 3

⇒ Substituting the given values:

⇒ 1 / 3 = 9 / IJ

⇒ IJ = 9 × 3

⇒ IJ = 27 cm

∴ The correct answer is 27 cm.

Additional Information

Properties of Similar Triangles

Corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same constant ratio.

Area of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(Δ1) ÷ Area(Δ2) = (Side1 ÷ Side2)².

Perimeter of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P1 ÷ P2 = Side1 ÷ Side2.

questions.q: Places A and B are 20 km apart on the highway. A car starts from A and another from B at the same time. If the cars travel in the same direction at different speeds, they meet in one hour. If they travelled towards each other, they met in 12 minutes. What are the speeds (in km/h) of two cars?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative speed in same direction (S₁ − S₂) = Distance ÷ Time = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 km/h

Relative speed in opposite direction (S₁ + S₂) = 20 ÷ (12/60) = 20 × 5 = 100 km/h

Speed of first car (S₁) = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (100 + 20) ÷ 2 = 60 km/h

Speed of second car (S₂) = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (100 − 20) ÷ 2 = 40 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 60, 40 km/h.

Alternate Method



Given:

Distance (D) = 20 km

Time in same direction (T₁) = 1 hour

Time in opposite direction (T₂) = 12 minutes = 12/60 hour = 1/5 hour

Formula Used:

Relative Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Relative Speed (Same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Relative Speed (Opposite direction) = S₁ + S₂

Calculations:

⇒ S₁ − S₂ = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 km/h --- (Equation 1)

⇒ S₁ + S₂ = 20 ÷ (1/5) = 20 × 5 = 100 km/h --- (Equation 2)

Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 2S₁ = 120

⇒ S₁ = 60 km/h

Substituting S₁ = 60 in Equation 2:

⇒ 60 + S₂ = 100

⇒ S₂ = 40 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 60, 40 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Time & Distance Rule

The time taken for two objects to meet is calculated by dividing the initial distance between them by their relative speed: Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed.

questions.q: If 45º and 65º are the angles of a triangle, then find the exterior angle of the third angle (remaining angle).

Shortcut Trick

According to the Exterior Angle Theorem, the exterior angle of a triangle is always equal to the sum of its two opposite (remote) interior angles.

The two given opposite interior angles are 45º and 65º.

Exterior angle of the third angle = 45º + 65º = 110º

∴ The correct answer is 110º.

Alternate Method

Given:

Two angles of a triangle are 45º and 65º.

Formula Used:

Sum of all interior angles of a triangle = 180º

Interior angle + Exterior angle = 180º (Linear Pair)

Calculations:

⇒ Let the three interior angles of the triangle be ∠A, ∠B, and ∠C.

⇒ Let ∠A = 65º and ∠B = 45º

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 65º + 45º + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 110º + ∠C = 180º

Additional Information

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is always strictly equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote (opposite) interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of a planar triangle is universally equal to 180º.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon (including a triangle), taking one at each vertex, is always 360º.

questions.q: A right triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is rotated about the sides of 3 cm to form a cone. The volume of the cone so formed is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a right-angled triangle is rotated about one of its perpendicular sides, that side becomes the height of the generated cone.

Here, the triangle is rotated about the 3 cm side, so Height (h) = 3 cm.

The other perpendicular side becomes the base radius, so Radius (r) = 4 cm.

Volume of the cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h = (1/3) × π × 4² × 3 = 16π cm³.

∴ The correct answer is 16π cm³.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sides of the right-angled triangle = 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm.

The triangle is rotated about the side of 3 cm.

Formula Used:

Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h



Calculations:

⇒ When the triangle is rotated about the 3 cm side, this side becomes the axis of rotation.

⇒ Height of the cone (h) = 3 cm

⇒ Radius of the base (r) = 4 cm

⇒ Slant height (l) = Hypotenuse = 5 cm

⇒ Volume of the cone = (1/3) × π × (4)² × 3

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × 16 × 3

⇒ Volume = 16π cm³

∴ The correct answer is 16π cm³.

Additional Information

Rotation about the other side

If the same right triangle was rotated about the 4 cm side instead, the height would be 4 cm and the radius would be 3 cm. The resulting volume would be (1/3) × π × 3² × 4 = 12π cm³.

Rotation about the hypotenuse

If the triangle is rotated about its hypotenuse (5 cm), it forms a double cone. The common radius of these cones is given by (Base × Perpendicular) ÷ Hypotenuse = (3 × 4) ÷ 5 = 2.4 cm.

Surface Areas of a Cone

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl and Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(r + l), where r is the base radius and l is the slant height.

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

questions.q: If x​ + (1)/(sqrt{x)} = 7, then the value of x + x1​ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If a + 1/a = k, then a² + 1/a² = k² − 2

Given: √x + 1/√x = 7

Here, a = √x and k = 7

x + 1/x = 7² − 2

x + 1/x = 49 − 2 = 47

∴ The correct answer is 47.

Alternate Method

Given:

√x + 1/√x = 7

Formula Used:

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

Calculations:

Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (√x + 1/√x)² = 7²

⇒ (√x)² + (1/√x)² + 2 × √x × (1/√x) = 49

⇒ x + 1/x + 2 = 49

⇒ x + 1/x = 49 − 2

⇒ x + 1/x = 47

∴ The correct answer is 47.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

If a + 1/a = k, then a³ + 1/a³ = k³ − 3k.

Algebraic Identity for Squares with Minus

If a − 1/a = k, then a² + 1/a² = k² + 2.

Higher Powers

If a + 1/a = k, then a⁴ + 1/a⁴ = (k² − 2)² − 2.

questions.q: A merchant has 1000 kg of sugar, part of which he sells at a 10% profit and the rest at a 40% profit. He gains 20% on the whole. The quantity sold at 40% profit is:
options: ​54331​ {kg}
​38331​ {kg}
​33331​ {kg}
​44331​ {kg}
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the rule of Alligation:

Ratio of quantity at 10% to quantity at 40% = (40 − 20) : (20 − 10)

Ratio = 20 : 10 = 2 : 1

Total parts = 2 + 1 = 3 parts

Quantity at 40% profit = 1 ÷ 3 × 1000 = 333 ¹/₃ kg

∴ The correct answer is 333 ¹/₃ kg.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total quantity of sugar = 1000 kg

Profit on first part = 10%

Profit on second part = 40%

Overall profit = 20%



Formula Used:

Overall Profit = (Q₁ × P₁ + Q₂ × P₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂)

Calculations:

Let the quantity of sugar sold at 40% profit be x kg.

⇒ Quantity of sugar sold at 10% profit = (1000 − x) kg.

⇒ Total profit on both parts equals the overall profit on the total mixture.

⇒ 10% of (1000 − x) + 40% of x = 20% of 1000

⇒ 0.1 × (1000 − x) + 0.4x = 0.2 × 1000

⇒ 100 − 0.1x + 0.4x = 200

⇒ 0.3x = 100

⇒ x = 100 ÷ 0.3

⇒ x = 1000 ÷ 3 = 333 ¹/₃ kg

∴ The correct answer is 333 ¹/₃ kg.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

When two items of different values are mixed, the ratio of their quantities is inversely proportional to the difference between their values and the mixture's mean value: Q₁ ÷ Q₂ = (P₂ − Mean) ÷ (Mean − P₁).

Weighted Average Method

Weighted average combines multiple sets by multiplying each value by its weight (quantity) and dividing by total weight: Aw = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

Profit & Loss on Mixtures

Overall profit or loss is calculated over the combined Cost Price. For items with identical Cost Price per unit, the profit percentages can be mixed using alligation directly on the total quantities.

questions.q: The concentrations of three acids, A, B, and C, are specified as 20%, 30%, and 40%, respectively. They are blended in a ratio of 3 : 5 : a, yielding a solution with a concentration of 30%. What is the value of 'a'?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the net deviation method from the mean mixture concentration (30%):

Deviation of Acid A = 3 × (20% − 30%) = −30%

Deviation of Acid B = 5 × (30% − 30%) = 0%

Deviation of Acid C = a × (40% − 30%) = +10a%

The net deviation must be zero ⇒ −30 + 0 + 10a = 0 ⇒ 10a = 30 ⇒ a = 3.

∴ The correct answer is a = 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Concentrations of Acid A, B, and C are 20%, 30%, and 40% respectively.

Ratio of their mixed quantities = 3 : 5 : a.

Concentration of the final blended mixture = 30%.

Concept Used:

Since Acid B has a concentration (30%) equal to the final mixture's target concentration, its presence does not alter the average concentration of the rest of the mixture. Thus, mixing Acid A and Acid C alone must also result in a 30% concentration. We can use the alligation method on A and C.



Calculations:

⇒ From the alligation rule, the required ratio of Quantity of A : Quantity of C is 1 : 1

⇒ 3 : a = 1 : 1

⇒ a = 3

Conventional Method:

⇒ Final Concentration = (CA × QA + CB × QB + CC × QC) ÷ (QA + QB + QC)

⇒ 30 = (20 × 3 + 30 × 5 + 40 × a) ÷ (3 + 5 + a)

⇒ 30 = (60 + 150 + 40a) ÷ (8 + a)

⇒ 30 × (8 + a) = 210 + 40a

⇒ 240 + 30a = 210 + 40a

⇒ 40a − 30a = 240 − 210

⇒ 10a = 30

⇒ a = 3

∴ The correct answer is a = 3.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

Used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given concentrations must be mixed to produce a desired mixture. Ratio = (Higher Value − Mean) : (Mean − Lower Value).

Weighted Average Formula

When mixing multiple quantities, the average concentration is the sum of the products of quantities and their concentrations divided by the total quantity: Cₘᵢₓ = (n₁c₁ + n₂c₂ + ...) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ...).

Replacement Method

When a volume 'V' of a mixture is repeatedly replaced by a pure ingredient 'n' times, the remaining quantity of the other component is: Final = Initial × [1 − (V ÷ Total)]ⁿ.

questions.q: Simplify 0.58times0.58+0.058+0.010.58times0.58times0.58−0.001​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The given expression follows the algebraic form of (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²).

Using the identity, this expression directly simplifies to (a − b).

Here, a = 0.58 and b = 0.1 (since 0.1³ = 0.001).

⇒ Result = 0.58 − 0.1 = 0.48

∴ The correct answer is 0.48.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = (0.58 × 0.58 × 0.58 − 0.001) ÷ (0.58 × 0.58 + 0.058 + 0.01)

Formula Used:

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

Calculation:

⇒ The numerator can be written as: (0.58)³ − (0.1)³

⇒ The denominator can be written as: (0.58)² + (0.58 × 0.1) + (0.1)²

⇒ Let a = 0.58 and b = 0.1

⇒ Expression = (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²)

⇒ Expression = [(a − b)(a² + ab + b²)] ÷ (a² + ab + b²)

⇒ Canceling the common term (a² + ab + b²) from numerator and denominator:

⇒ Expression = a − b

⇒ Substituting the values back: 0.58 − 0.1 = 0.48

∴ The correct answer is 0.48.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). If a simplification expression is written as (a³ + b³) ÷ (a² − ab + b²), the result will simply be (a + b).

Difference of Squares Identity

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). This is commonly used to simplify fractions involving square numbers.

Perfect Square Simplification

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab. This pattern often appears in fractional expressions where the denominator is ab, making the direct answer 4.

questions.q: Ravi's salary was increased by 50%. After some time, his new salary was also increased by 50%. Find his gain percentage on the salary.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a value is successively increased by x% and y%, the net percentage change is calculated using the successive percentage formula:

Net % Change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, both increments are 50% (so x = 50, y = 50).

Net % Change = 50 + 50 + (50 × 50) ÷ 100 = 100 + 25 = 125%

∴ The correct answer is 125%.

Alternate Method



Given:

First salary increase = 50%

Second salary increase = 50%

Formula Used:

Gain Percentage = (Total Gain ÷ Initial Salary) × 100%

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial salary of Ravi be 100 units.

⇒ After the first 50% increase, salary = 100 + (50% of 100) = 150 units.

⇒ After the second 50% increase, salary = 150 + (50% of 150) = 150 + 75 = 225 units.

⇒ Total Gain = Final Salary − Initial Salary = 225 − 100 = 125 units.

⇒ Gain Percentage = (125 ÷ 100) × 100% = 125%.

∴ The correct answer is 125%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100]%. Remember to use a negative sign if it involves a decrease.

Multiplier Method (Fractional Equivalent)

A 50% increase means the new value becomes 150% (or 3/2) of the original base. Two successive 50% increases mean multiplying the base by (3/2) × (3/2) = 9/4. This represents an overall increase of 5/4 over the initial value, which is exactly 125%.

Base Change Implication

A common exam mistake is simply adding the percentages directly (50% + 50% = 100%). However, successive calculations must factor in that the second percentage increase operates on an already enlarged base, which intrinsically leads to a higher net gain.

questions.q: If cotθ = 4/3, then evaluate: (secθ(1 + cot²θ)(cosec²θ - cot²θ)) / cosec³θ.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simplify the expression directly using basic trigonometric identities:

We know that (1 + cot²θ) = cosec²θ and (cosec²θ − cot²θ) = 1

Given expression = (secθ × cosec²θ × 1) ÷ cosec³θ

⇒ secθ ÷ cosecθ = (1 / cosθ) ÷ (1 / sinθ) = sinθ / cosθ = tanθ

Since cotθ = 4/3, we get tanθ = 1 / cotθ = 3/4.

∴ The correct answer is 3/4.

Alternate Method

Given:

cotθ = 4/3 = Base / Perpendicular



Calculations:

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(Base² + Perpendicular²) = √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5

⇒ secθ = Hypotenuse / Base = 5/4

⇒ cosecθ = Hypotenuse / Perpendicular = 5/3

Substitute these values into the given expression:

⇒ Numerator = secθ × (1 + cot²θ) × (cosec²θ − cot²θ)

⇒ Numerator = (5/4) × (1 + 16/9) × (25/9 − 16/9)

⇒ Numerator = (5/4) × (25/9) × (9/9) = 125/36

⇒ Denominator = cosec³θ = (5/3)³ = 125/27

⇒ Expression value = (125/36) ÷ (125/27) = (125/36) × (27/125)

⇒ Expression value = 27/36 = 3/4

∴ The correct answer is 3/4.

Additional Information

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

The three primary square identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

The reciprocal of sine is cosecant (cosecθ = 1/sinθ), cosine is secant (secθ = 1/cosθ), and tangent is cotangent (cotθ = 1/tanθ).

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is always equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

questions.q: If (77⁷⁷+ 77) is divided by 78, then the remainder will be:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the property of remainders, evaluate the expression term by term.

When aⁿ is divided by (a + 1), the remainder is −1 if n is odd.

Here, 77⁷⁷ ÷ 78 gives a remainder of (−1)⁷⁷ = −1.

The second term 77 ÷ 78 gives a remainder of 77.

Total remainder = −1 + 77 = 76.

∴ The correct answer is 76.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = 77⁷⁷ + 77

Divisor = 78

Formula Used:

If P(x) = (x − 1)ⁿ is divided by x, the remainder is (−1)ⁿ.

Remainder of (A + B) ÷ C = [ (Remainder of A ÷ C) + (Remainder of B ÷ C) ]

Calculation:

⇒ Break the expression and divide each term by 78 separately.

⇒ (77⁷⁷ + 77) ÷ 78 = [(78 − 1)⁷⁷ ÷ 78] + [77 ÷ 78]

⇒ Remainder of (78 − 1)⁷⁷ ÷ 78 = (−1)⁷⁷ = −1

⇒ Remainder of 77 ÷ 78 = 77

⇒ Total Remainder = −1 + 77

⇒ Final Remainder = 76

∴ The correct answer is 76.

Additional Information

Remainder of aⁿ ÷ (a + 1)

If n is even, the remainder is always 1. If n is odd, the remainder is a (or −1).

Remainder of aⁿ ÷ (a − 1)

For any natural number n, the remainder is always 1.

Negative Remainder Concept

When a calculation gives a negative remainder −R, the actual positive remainder is (Divisor − R).

questions.q: Two successive discounts of 40% and 30% are equal to a single discount of:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent discount is given by the direct formula:

Equivalent Discount = [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%

⇒ Equivalent Discount = [40 + 30 − (40 × 30) ÷ 100]%

⇒ Equivalent Discount = [70 − 1200 ÷ 100]%

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 70 − 12 = 58%

∴ The correct answer is 58%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Two successive discounts = 40% and 30%

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100



Calculations:

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) of the article be 100.

⇒ Price after the first discount of 40% = 100 − (40% of 100) = 100 − 40 = 60

⇒ Price after the second discount of 30% = 60 − (30% of 60) = 60 − 18 = 42

⇒ The final Selling Price (SP) becomes 42.

⇒ Total Discount given = Original MP − Final SP

⇒ Total Discount = 100 − 42 = 58

⇒ Since the base MP is 100, the equivalent discount percentage is exactly 58%.

∴ The correct answer is 58%.

Additional Information

Successive Discount for Three Items

For three successive discounts a%, b%, and c%, the final selling price is calculated as: SP = MP × (1 − a ÷ 100) × (1 − b ÷ 100) × (1 − c ÷ 100).

Marked Price and Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of the item. Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount.

Single vs Successive Discounts

A single flat discount of (x + y)% will always result in a lower selling price (i.e., a better deal for the buyer) compared to two successive discounts of x% and y% applied one after the other on the same article.

questions.q: In a circle of radius 5√13 cm, a chord is at a distance of 10 cm from the centre of the circle. Find the length (in cm) of the chord.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The length of a chord in a circle can be directly found using the formula: L = 2 × √(r² − d²)

Where r = radius of the circle, d = perpendicular distance from the centre.

Here, r = 5√13 cm and d = 10 cm.

L = 2 × √[(5√13)² − 10²] = 2 × √(325 − 100)

L = 2 × √225 = 2 × 15 = 30 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 30 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the circle (OA) = 5√13 cm

Distance from the centre to the chord (OM) = 10 cm

•
•
• O M A B 5√13 cm 10 cm Distance OM = 10 cm, Radius OA = 5√13 cm Chord AB = 2 × AM = 30 cm

Formula Used:

By Pythagoras Theorem in a right-angled triangle:

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord. So, AB = 2 × AM.

Calculations:

In right-angled triangle OMA:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ (5√13)² = 10² + AM²

⇒ 25 × 13 = 100 + AM²

⇒ 325 = 100 + AM²

⇒ AM² = 325 − 100 = 225

⇒ AM = √225 = 15 cm

Now, finding the length of the entire chord AB:

⇒ AB = 2 × AM

⇒ AB = 2 × 15 = 30 cm

∴ The correct answer is 30 cm.

Additional Information

Properties of a Chord

A perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord. Conversely, the line joining the centre of a circle to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord.

Equal Chords Property

Chords of equal length in a circle subtend equal angles at the centre, and they are always equidistant from the centre.

Longest Chord

The diameter is the longest chord of a circle. Its length is exactly double the radius (D = 2 × r) and its distance from the centre is directly zero.

questions.q: What annual instalment will discharge a debt of ₹26,160 due in 4 years at 6% simple interest p.a.?
questions.solution:
